 144:     return _pop(Y, ["bare", "m1", "m2", "m3"], _task_ids(n),
 145:                 _task_ids(n)[:n_dev], meta={})

 147: 
 148: def gen_C6_cost_kills_gain(seed):        # dev signal flips on eval; net utility negative
 149:     """Stratum A members look excellent on dev (m_risky 0.9) but the mechanism
 150:     FLIPS on eval (m_risky 0.1 on A) - realistic distribution drift. The frozen
 151:     policy is lured: D REFUTED (pi worse than dev-fixed) and E REFUTED (net
 152:     utility negative under lambda=1), while naive dev metrics looked fine."""
 153:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 154:     n_dev, n_ev = 100, 500
 155:     n = n_dev + n_ev
 156:     stratum = np.array(["A"] * n)
 157:     stratum[::2] = "B"
 158:     p_risky_A = np.where(np.arange(n) < n_dev, 0.9, 0.1)   # drift: dev 0.9 -> eval 0.1
 159:     Y = np.vstack([
 160:         (rng.random(n) < 0.5).astype(float),                        # bare
 161:         (rng.random(n) < np.where(stratum == "A", p_risky_A, 0.0)).astype(float),
 162:         (rng.random(n) < 0.55).astype(float),                       # m_steady
 163:     ])
 164:     meta = {t: {"stratum": stratum[i]} for i, t in enumerate(_task_ids(n))}
 165:     return _pop(Y, ["bare", "m_risky", "m_steady"], _task_ids(n),
 166:                 _task_ids(n)[:n_dev], meta=meta)

 169: def gen_C7_headroom_from_bestfixed_drop(seed):  # headroom inflated by weak members
 170:     """bare is strong, all generated members weak-but-diverse -> headroom is
 171:     positive ONLY because best-fixed fell below bare; a naive reading 'positive
 172:     headroom => deploy a member' is the trap under test (B SUPPORTED but bare is
 173:     best; D/E must NOT support deploying a generated member)."""
 174:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 175:     n_dev, n_ev = 60, 160
 176:     n = n_dev + n_ev
 177:     Y = np.empty((4, n))
 178:     Y[0] = (rng.random(n) < 0.80).astype(float)      # bare strong
 179:     Y[1] = (rng.random(n) < 0.55).astype(float)
 180:     Y[2] = (rng.random(n) < 0.60).astype(float)
 181:     Y[3] = (rng.random(n) < 0.58).astype(float)
 182:     return _pop(Y, ["bare", "w1", "w2", "w3"], _task_ids(n), _task_ids(n)[:n_dev], meta={})

 185: def gen_C8_integrity_violation(seed, mode):      # corrupted inputs (S1 must catch)
 186:     """One mechanism, two violation modes: missing member cells, corrupted judge
 187:     (verdict flips on 10% of cells, surfaced as judge-replay mismatches). S1/A
 188:     must REFUTE while naive metrics look healthy."""
 189:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 190:     n = 120
 191:     Y = (rng.random((3, n)) < 0.6).astype(float)
 192:     member_ids = ["bare", "a", "b"]
 193:     replays, dups = 0, 0
 194:     if mode == "missing_member":
 195:         Y[2, :30] = np.nan
 196:     elif mode == "corrupt_judge":
 197:         flip = rng.random((3, n)) < 0.10
 198:         Y = np.where(flip, 1 - Y, Y)
 199:         replays = int(flip.sum())
 200:     pop = _pop(Y, member_ids, _task_ids(Y.shape[1]), _task_ids(24)[:24])
 201:     pop.judge_replay_mismatches = replays
 202:     pop.duplicate_keys = dups
 203:     return pop

 206: # ---- repeat-based generators (v2): S3 paths + ranking-vs-complementarity ----
 207: 
 208: def _repeat_pop(Y, member_ids, tasks, condition, repeat_index, seed,
 209:                 dev_ids=None):
 210:     """One same-condition repeat with independent execution noise from `seed`."""
 211:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1000 * repeat_index)
 212:     Yr = np.array(Y, dtype=float, copy=True)
 213:     noise = np.isnan(Yr) | (Yr < 0)          # cells marked -1 are stochastic
 214:     if noise.any():
 215:         Yr[noise] = (rng.random(int(noise.sum())) < 0.5).astype(float)
 216:     return Population(
 217:         member_ids=member_ids,
 218:         source_hashes=[f"h{i}" for i in range(len(member_ids))],
 219:         tasks=tasks, Y=Yr, condition=dict(condition), has_bare=True,
 220:         dev_task_ids=dev_ids or [], task_meta={},
 221:         calls={}, calls_status="not_provided")
 222: 
 223: 
 224: _STOCH = -1.0   # sentinel: cell is stochastic Bernoulli(0.5), drawn per repeat
 225: 
 226: 
 227: def gen_C9_global_dominance(seed):       # ranking != complementarity
 228:     """dom is deterministically correct on EVERY task, a only on 30-44, bare is
 229:     stochastic Bernoulli(0.5) per repeat. dom is expectation-best everywhere ->
 230:     H_stable = 0 (complementarity REFUTED) even though the ranking difference
 231:     dom-a is perfectly stable (SUPPORTED) and naive pair scanning 'finds' it.
 232:     """
 233:     n, n_dev = 60, 20
 234:     tasks = _task_ids(n)
 235:     Y = np.full((3, n), _STOCH)
 236:     Y[0, :] = _STOCH                       # bare: stochastic per repeat
 237:     Y[1, 30:45] = 1.0                      # a: correct on tasks 30-44 only
 238:     Y[1, :] = np.where(Y[1] == _STOCH, 0.0, Y[1])
 239:     Y[2, :] = 1.0                          # dom: always correct
 240:     return {f"r{r}": _repeat_pop(Y, ["bare", "a", "dom"], tasks,
 241:                                  {"c": "synthetic", "timeout": 60}, r, seed,
 242:                                  dev_ids=tasks[:n_dev])
 243:             for r in range(3)}
 244: 
 245: 
 246: def gen_C10_crossover_complementarity(seed):   # equal means, real interaction
 247:     """m_sql deterministically correct on the 30 A tasks, m_text on the 30 B
 248:     tasks, bare stochastic. Mean accuracies are equal (0.5 vs 0.5) so no stable
 249:     MEAN difference exists (ranking INSUFFICIENT), yet per-task expectation
 250:     crosses: H_stable = 0.5 (complementarity SUPPORTED) and the visible stratum
 251:     makes it selectable (D/E SUPPORTED). The dev split covers BOTH strata
 252:     (10 A + 10 B tasks) - a single-stratum dev split could not learn routing."""
 253:     n = 60
 254:     tasks = _task_ids(n)
 255:     Y = np.full((3, n), _STOCH)
 256:     Y[0, :] = _STOCH                       # bare stochastic
 257:     Y[1, 0:30] = 1.0                       # m_sql on A tasks
 258:     Y[1, 30:] = 0.0
 259:     Y[2, 0:30] = 0.0
 260:     Y[2, 30:] = 1.0                        # m_text on B tasks
 261:     meta = {t: {"stratum": "A" if i < 30 else "B"} for i, t in enumerate(tasks)}
 262:     dev_ids = tasks[0:10] + tasks[30:40]   # both strata represented in dev
 263:     pops = {}
 264:     for r in range(3):
 265:         p = _repeat_pop(Y, ["bare", "m_sql", "m_text"], tasks,
 266:                         {"c": "synthetic", "timeout": 60}, r, seed,
 267:                         dev_ids=dev_ids)
 268:         p.task_meta = meta
 269:         pops[f"r{r}"] = p
 270:     return pops
 271: 
 272: 
 273: def gen_C11_condition_mixing(seed):      # one 'repeat' under a different condition
 274:     """Three matrices where the third was produced under timeout=61, not 60.
 275:     These are different execution conditions, not matched repeats: S3 must
 276:     refuse the merge and abstain, regardless of how clean the matrices look."""
 277:     n, n_dev = 60, 20
 278:     tasks = _task_ids(n)
 279:     Y = np.zeros((3, n))
 280:     Y[0, 0:24] = 1.0                       # bare
 281:     Y[1, 0:36] = 1.0                       # a
 282:     Y[2, 18:48] = 1.0                      # b (crossover with a)
 283:     Y[2, 0:18] = 0.0
 284:     pops = {}
 285:     for r in range(3):
 286:         cond = {"c": "synthetic", "timeout": 61 if r == 2 else 60}
 287:         pops[f"r{r}"] = Population(
 288:             member_ids=["bare", "a", "b"],
 289:             source_hashes=[f"h{i}" for i in range(3)],
 290:             tasks=tasks, Y=np.array(Y, dtype=float, copy=True),
 291:             condition=cond, has_bare=True, dev_task_ids=tasks[:n_dev],
 292:             task_meta={}, calls={}, calls_status="not_provided")
 293:     return pops
 294: 
 295: 
 296: def gen_C12_cloned_repeats(seed):        # identical matrices = unverifiable repeats
 297:     """Three byte-identical matrices (deterministic members). Independent
 298:     executions cannot be verified; S3 must abstain even though every other
 299:     signal (integrity, coverage) looks healthy."""
 300:     n, n_dev = 60, 20
 301:     tasks = _task_ids(n)
 302:     Y = np.zeros((3, n))
 303:     Y[0, 48:60] = 1.0                      # bare correct on 48-59
 304:     Y[1, 18:48] = 1.0                      # a on 18-47
 305:     Y[2, 0:36] = 1.0                       # dom on 0-35
 306:     pops = {}
 307:     for r in range(3):
 308:         pops[f"r{r}"] = Population(
 309:             member_ids=["bare", "a", "dom"],
 310:             source_hashes=[f"h{i}" for i in range(3)],
 311:             tasks=tasks, Y=np.array(Y, dtype=float, copy=True),
 312:             condition={"c": "synthetic", "timeout": 60}, has_bare=True,
 313:             dev_task_ids=tasks[:n_dev], task_meta={}, calls={},
 314:             calls_status="not_provided")
 315:     return pops

 317: 
 318: REPEAT_CLASSES = {
 319:     "C9": gen_C9_global_dominance,
 320:     "C10": gen_C10_crossover_complementarity,
 321:     "C11": gen_C11_condition_mixing,
 322:     "C12": gen_C12_cloned_repeats,
 323: }

 326: # ---- frozen package ---------------------------------------------------------
 327: 
 328: # Expected states, frozen from the generating mechanisms (NOT from running the
 329: # diagnostics). S1/A for clean controls = SUPPORTED; C = INSUFFICIENT everywhere
 330: # in v1 classes (single-shot synthetic data has no matched repeats), likewise
 331: # C_comp (the complementarity estimand needs repeats by definition).
 332: _CLEAN_A = SUPPORTED
 333: _CLEAN_C = INSUFFICIENT
 334: CLASSES = [
 335:     ("C1", "identical outputs, different code",
 336:      lambda s: gen_C1_common_output(s),
 337:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": REFUTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 338:       "D": INSUFFICIENT, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 339:     ("C2", "random one-shot gap, no pre-execution signal",
 340:      lambda s: gen_C2_random_gap_no_signal(s),
 341:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 342:       "D": INSUFFICIENT, "E": SUPPORTED}),
 343:     ("C3", "single dominant member, strata-varying gap",
 344:      lambda s: gen_C3_single_dominant(s),
 345:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 346:       "D": REFUTED, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 347:     ("C4", "stable complementarity identified by visible stratum (POSITIVE control)",
 348:      lambda s: gen_C4_real_complementarity(s),
 349:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 350:       "D": SUPPORTED, "E": SUPPORTED}),
 351:     ("C5", "real complementarity, Z cannot identify it (abstention control)",
 352:      lambda s: gen_C5_complementarity_unidentifiable(s),
 353:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 354:       "D": REFUTED, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 355:     ("C6", "dev/eval drift flips Z signal; no coverage, net utility negative",
 356:      lambda s: gen_C6_cost_kills_gain(s),
 357:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 358:       "D": REFUTED, "E": REFUTED}),
 359:     ("C7", "headroom driven by best-fixed drop; bare remains best",
 360:      lambda s: gen_C7_headroom_from_bestfixed_drop(s),
 361:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 362:       "D": INSUFFICIENT, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 363:     ("C8", "integrity violations caught by S1",
 364:      None,   # per-instance generator mode set below
 365:      {"A": REFUTED, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": _CLEAN_C, "C_comp": _CLEAN_C,
 366:       "D": INSUFFICIENT, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 367:     # ---- v2 repeat-based classes (S3 paths) ----
 368:     ("C9", "global dominance with repeats: stable ranking SUPPORTED, "
 369:            "complementarity REFUTED (H_stable = 0)",
 370:      lambda s: gen_C9_global_dominance(s),
 371:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": REFUTED, "C": SUPPORTED, "C_comp": REFUTED,
 372:       "D": INSUFFICIENT, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 373:     ("C10", "crossover interaction with repeats: equal means (ranking "
 374:             "INSUFFICIENT) but real complementarity SUPPORTED",
 375:      lambda s: gen_C10_crossover_complementarity(s),
 376:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": INSUFFICIENT, "C_comp": SUPPORTED,
 377:       "D": SUPPORTED, "E": SUPPORTED}),
 378:     ("C11", "condition-mixing trap: one 'repeat' under a different timeout",
 379:      lambda s: gen_C11_condition_mixing(s),
 380:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": INSUFFICIENT, "C_comp": INSUFFICIENT,
 381:       "D": INSUFFICIENT, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 382:     ("C12", "cloned-repeats trap: identical matrices, independence unverifiable",
 383:      lambda s: gen_C12_cloned_repeats(s),
 384:      {"A": _CLEAN_A, "B": SUPPORTED, "C": INSUFFICIENT, "C_comp": INSUFFICIENT,
 385:       "D": INSUFFICIENT, "E": INSUFFICIENT}),
 386: ]
 387: C8_MODES = ["missing_member", "corrupt_judge"]
 388: 
 389: 
 390: def build_package() -> dict:
 391:     """Freeze all controls + expected states; return manifest dict."""
 392:     controls = []
 393:     for cid, desc, gen, expected in CLASSES:
 394:         for instance in (1, 2):
 395:             if cid == "C8":
 396:                 mode = C8_MODES[instance - 1]
 397:                 pop = gen_C8_integrity_violation(1000 + instance, mode)
 398:                 d = f"{desc} [{mode}]"
 399:                 repeats = 1
 400:             elif cid in REPEAT_CLASSES:
 401:                 pops = REPEAT_CLASSES[cid](stable_seed(cid, instance))
 402:                 pop = pops[sorted(pops)[0]]
 403:                 d = desc
 404:                 repeats = len(pops)
 405:             else:
 406:                 pop = gen(stable_seed(cid, instance))
 407:                 d = desc
 408:                 repeats = 1
 409:             controls.append({
 410:                 "cid": cid, "cls": desc, "instance": instance,
 411:                 "instance_phase": "calibration" if instance == 1 else "blinded",
 412:                 "description": d,
 413:                 "expected": expected,
 414:                 "n_members": len(pop.member_ids), "n_tasks": len(pop.tasks),
 415:                 "n_repeats": repeats,
 416:             })
 417:     manifest = {
 418:         "package": "diagnostics control package v2 (v1 frozen 16 + C9-C12 "
 419:                    "repeat-based classes per the 2026-09-15 external review)",
 420:         "n_classes": len(CLASSES), "n_controls": len(controls),
 421:         "calibration": [c["cid"] + f"#{c['instance']}" for c in controls if c["instance_phase"] == "calibration"],
 422:         "blinded": [c["cid"] + f"#{c['instance']}" for c in controls if c["instance_phase"] == "blinded"],
 423:         "controls": controls,
 424:         "notes": "expected states derive from the analytic generating mechanisms; "
 425:                  "C2/C6/C7 D/E expectations assume the frozen 1-call policy; "
 426:                  "auditor challenges are re-executed from the frozen spec in the "
 427:                  "blinded phase with spec+code hash binding. v1 classes keep "
 428:                  "their frozen expectations unchanged.",
 429:     }
 430:     manifest["manifest_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(
 431:         json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
 432:     return manifest

 435: def get_control(cid: str, instance: int):
 436:     """Return a Population (single-shot classes) or {repeat_key: Population}
 437:     (repeat-based classes C9-C12) for the given control instance."""
 438:     if cid in REPEAT_CLASSES:
 439:         return REPEAT_CLASSES[cid](stable_seed(cid, instance))
 440:     for c, _, gen, _ in [(x[0], x[1], x[2], x[3]) for x in CLASSES]:
 441:         if c == cid:
 442:             if cid == "C8":
 443:                 return gen_C8_integrity_violation(stable_seed(cid, instance),
 444:                                                   C8_MODES[instance - 1])
 445:             return gen(stable_seed(cid, instance))
 446:     raise KeyError(cid)

1: """Spec-faithful executors for the pre-committed auditor challenges (CH1, CH2).
   2: 
   3: The challenge contracts live in review-stage/astra_20260915/challenge_spec.json
   4: (SHA256 recorded in challenge_spec.sha256). Both challenges are fully
   5: deterministic generating rules, so they can be RE-EXECUTED under the current
   6: diagnostics code instead of replaying a stored result file.
   7: 
   8: History note (recorded per the 2026-09-15 external review): the archived
   9: astra_challenges_result.json was produced by an earlier, unverified challenge
  10: implementation whose stored numbers contradict the spec they claim to execute
  11: (e.g. CH2 best_fixed_accuracy = 0.94, unreachable under the spec's generating
  12: rule, which forces 0.79). Re-execution from the spec under hash-bound current
  13: code supersedes that file; the historical file is retained for provenance and
  14: can only be used as a labeled historical replay (cli.verify-challenges).
  15: """
  16: from __future__ import annotations
  17: 
  18: import hashlib
  19: import json
  20: from pathlib import Path
  21: 
  22: import numpy as np
  23: 
  24: from experiment.diagnostics.core import Population
  25: 
  26: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
  27: SPEC_PATH = ROOT / "review-stage/astra_20260915/challenge_spec.json"
  28: 
  29: 
  30: def spec_sha256() -> str:
  31:     return hashlib.sha256(SPEC_PATH.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
  32: 
  33: 
  34: def code_binding() -> dict:
  35:     """Hash every diagnostics module that determines challenge outcomes, so a
  36:     stored or transmitted result can be bound to the code that produced it."""
  37:     import experiment.diagnostics.core as core
  38:     import experiment.diagnostics.challenges as ch
  39:     out = {}
  40:     for mod in (core, ch):
  41:         out[mod.__name__] = hashlib.sha256(
  42:             Path(mod.__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
  43:     return out
  44: 
  45: 
  46: def _pop_from_rules(Y: np.ndarray, member_ids: list[str], meta: dict,
  47:                     dev_ids: list[str], n_total: int) -> Population:
  48:     return Population(
  49:         member_ids=member_ids,
  50:         source_hashes=[f"challenge:{m}" for m in member_ids],
  51:         tasks=[f"ch_task{i}" for i in range(n_total)],
  52:         Y=np.asarray(Y, dtype=float),
  53:         condition={"target": "deterministic_rule", "repeat": 0, "no_cache": False,
  54:                    "judge": "challenge_spec"},
  55:         has_bare=True, dev_task_ids=dev_ids, task_meta=meta, calls={},
  56:         calls_status="not_provided")
  57: 
  58: 
  59: def build_ch1() -> Population:
  60:     """Three-way visible complementarity under severe stratum-prevalence shift.
  61: 
  62:     Spec: 4 members (bare, mA, mB, mC); 1200 tasks = 600 dev (A=480, B=90,
  63:     C=30) then 600 eval (A=60, B=270, C=270). Per stratum, task ordinal r
  64:     (contiguous across dev then eval; all dev counts are multiples of 10, so
  65:     per-split or global ordinals coincide): bare Y=1 iff r%10<5; the stratum's
  66:     winner (mA/mB/mC) Y=1 iff r%10<9; the other members Y=1 iff r%10<2.
  67:     """
  68:     dev_counts = {"A": 480, "B": 90, "C": 30}
  69:     ev_counts = {"A": 60, "B": 270, "C": 270}
  70:     strata = (["A"] * dev_counts["A"] + ["B"] * dev_counts["B"] + ["C"] * dev_counts["C"]
  71:               + ["A"] * ev_counts["A"] + ["B"] * ev_counts["B"] + ["C"] * ev_counts["C"])
  72:     n = len(strata)
  73:     winners = {"A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 3}      # column index of the stratum winner
  74:     Y = np.zeros((4, n))
  75:     ordinal = {s: 0 for s in "ABC"}
  76:     for j, s in enumerate(strata):
  77:         r = ordinal[s]
  78:         ordinal[s] += 1
  79:         Y[0, j] = 1.0 if r % 10 < 5 else 0.0
  80:         for m in (1, 2, 3):
  81:             Y[m, j] = (1.0 if r % 10 < 9 else 0.0) if m == winners[s] else \
  82:                       (1.0 if r % 10 < 2 else 0.0)
  83:     meta = {f"ch_task{j}": {"stratum": s} for j, s in enumerate(strata)}
  84:     dev_ids = [f"ch_task{j}" for j in range(600)]
  85:     return _pop_from_rules(Y, ["bare", "mA", "mB", "mC"], meta, dev_ids, n)
  86: 
  87: 
  88: def build_ch2() -> Population:
  89:     """Stable visible routing with bare-correlated errors that reverse
  90:     cost-sensitive utility.
  91: 
  92:     Spec: 3 members (bare, mA, mB); 2000 tasks = 1000 dev (800 A then 200 B)
  93:     then 1000 eval (500 A then 500 B). A tasks: (bare, mA, mB) = (0, 1, 0).
  94:     B tasks, first 60%: (0, 0, 1); last 40%: (1, 1, 0). The within-B subcase is
  95:     NOT exposed as metadata.
  96:     """
  97:     dev = [("A", (0, 1, 0))] * 800 + [("B", (0, 0, 1))] * 120 + [("B", (1, 1, 0))] * 80
  98:     ev = [("A", (0, 1, 0))] * 500 + [("B", (0, 0, 1))] * 300 + [("B", (1, 1, 0))] * 200
  99:     seq = dev + ev
 100:     n = len(seq)
 101:     Y = np.array([rule for _, rule in seq], dtype=float).T       # (3, n)
 102:     meta = {f"ch_task{j}": {"stratum": s} for j, (s, _) in enumerate(seq)}
 103:     dev_ids = [f"ch_task{j}" for j in range(1000)]
 104:     return _pop_from_rules(Y, ["bare", "mA", "mB"], meta, dev_ids, n)
 105: 
 106: 
 107: BUILDERS = {"CH1": build_ch1, "CH2": build_ch2}

 114: def execute_challenges(cls_runner) -> dict:
 115:     """Run every challenge in the frozen spec with the CURRENT code.
 116: 
 117:     cls_runner: callable Population -> {"A":..., "B":..., "C":..., "D":..., "E":...}
 118:     Returns a result dict bound to the spec hash and the diagnostics code hashes.
 119:     """
 120:     spec = load_spec()

  31: @dataclass
  32: class Population:
  33:     """Members x task outcome matrix for one execution condition c.

  35:     Y[i, j] in {0.0, 1.0}; NaN = missing (kept in the denominator, never imputed).
  36:     members[0] is the bare reference when has_bare.

  55:     @property

  76:             "vectors_per_gen_incl_bare": round(len(vecs) / max(1, denom), 4),

  81: # ---------------------------------------------------------------- S1 integrity
  82: 
  83: # Judge-replay evidence must state whether the replay was actually executed;
  84: # "not executed" must never be rendered as "check passed".
  85: JUDGE_REPLAY_EXECUTED = "executed"
  86: JUDGE_REPLAY_NOT_EXECUTED = "not_executed"
  87: JUDGE_REPLAY_INFEASIBLE = "infeasible"

  89: 
  90: def _normalize_judge_replay(judge_replay) -> dict:
  91:     """Accept a status dict or a bare mismatch count (count => executed)."""
  92:     if isinstance(judge_replay, dict):
  93:         status = judge_replay.get("status", JUDGE_REPLAY_EXECUTED)
  94:         mism = judge_replay.get("mismatches")
  95:         return {"status": status, "mismatches": mism}
  96:     return {"status": JUDGE_REPLAY_EXECUTED, "mismatches": int(judge_replay)}

  98: 
  99: def s1_integrity(manifest: dict, pop: Population, judge_replay,
 100:                  duplicate_keys: int, hash_conflicts: list[str]) -> dict:
 101:     """Plan 3.A (v2): manifest consistency, judge replay (with execution state),
 102:     identity uniqueness.
 103: 
 104:     Check values: True = passed, False = violated (blocks), None = could not be
 105:     run (forces INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, never SUPPORTED).
 106:     """
 107:     jr = _normalize_judge_replay(judge_replay)
 108:     if jr["status"] == JUDGE_REPLAY_EXECUTED:
 109:         judge_check = int(jr["mismatches"] or 0) == 0
 110:     else:
 111:         judge_check = None          # not run: cannot claim consistency
 112:     missing_cells = int(np.isnan(pop.Y).sum())
 113:     missing_frac = missing_cells / pop.Y.size if pop.Y.size else 0.0
 114:     checks = {
 115:         "manifest_member_match": manifest["member_ids"] == pop.member_ids,
 116:         "manifest_task_match": manifest["task_ids"] == pop.tasks,
 117:         "judge_replay_consistent": judge_check,
 118:         "no_duplicate_keys": duplicate_keys == 0,
 119:         "no_source_hash_conflict": not hash_conflicts,
 120:         "missing_cells_le_1pct": missing_frac <= 0.01,
 121:     }
 122:     blocked = [k for k, ok in checks.items() if ok is False]
 123:     not_run = [k for k, ok in checks.items() if ok is None]
 124:     if blocked:
 125:         state = REFUTED
 126:     elif not_run:
 127:         state = INSUFFICIENT        # verification missing != verification passed
 128:     else:
 129:         state = SUPPORTED
 130:     return {
 131:         "state": state, "checks": checks, "blocked": blocked, "not_run": not_run,
 132:         "judge_replay_status": jr["status"],
 133:         "judge_replay_mismatches": jr["mismatches"],
 134:         "missing_cells": missing_cells, "missing_frac": round(missing_frac, 6),
 135:         "duplicate_keys": duplicate_keys,
 136:         "source_hash_conflicts": hash_conflicts,
 137:         "minimal_missing_evidence":
 138:             ([f"repair {k} then re-run" for k in blocked] +
 139:              [f"execute or bind evidence for {k}" for k in not_run]),
 140:     }

 143: def digest_file(path: Path) -> str:
 144:     return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

 146: 
 147: 
 148: def _nanmean(arr, axis):
 149:     with warnings.catch_warnings():
 150:         warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
 151:         return np.nanmean(arr, axis=axis)
 152: 
 153: 
 154: def _acc(v) -> float:
 155:     """Recorded success rate: unknown/missing cells stay in the denominator and
 156:     count as not-correct (conservative, per the frozen propagation rule).
 157: 
 158:     This is a *recorded*-outcome rate, NOT a hypothesis-free estimate of the
 159:     rate over unknown true correctness. Missing counts and pair-level
 160:     imputation bounds (see _missing_bounds_delta) are reported alongside every
 161:     comparison so missingness can never silently create or destroy a
 162:     difference."""
 163:     v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
 164:     return float(np.nansum(v)) / len(v)
 165: 
 166: 
 167: def _accs_rows(Y: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
 168:     return np.nansum(Y, axis=1) / Y.shape[1]

 171: # ------------------------------------------------------------ S2 decomposition
 172: 
 173: def s2_decomposition(pop: Population, n_boot: int = 4000, seed: int = 20260915) -> dict:
 174:     """Plan 3.B: oracle / best-fixed / dev-fixed / bare on ONE execution matrix.
 175: 
 176:     Paired task bootstrap (strata = unique task strata key when metadata provides
 177:     a database/subject grouping, else plain task resample). CI > 0 -> SUPPORTED
 178:     restricted to "this matrix has unused single-shot coverage".
 179:     """
 180:     Y = pop.Y
 181:     n_t = Y.shape[1]
 182:     oracle_per_task = np.nanmax(Y, axis=0)
 183:     accs = {m: _acc(Y[i]) for i, m in enumerate(pop.member_ids)}
 184:     best_fixed_m = max(accs, key=accs.get)
 185:     best_fixed = float(accs[best_fixed_m])
 186:     oracle = float(np.nansum(oracle_per_task) / n_t)
 187:     headroom = oracle - best_fixed
 188: 
 189:     dev_fixed_m, dev_fixed = None, None
 190:     if pop.dev_task_ids:
 191:         dev_idx = [pop.tasks.index(t) for t in pop.dev_task_ids if t in pop.tasks]
 192:         if dev_idx:
 193:             dev_accs = {m: _acc(Y[i, dev_idx]) for i, m in enumerate(pop.member_ids)}
 194:             dev_fixed_m = max(dev_accs, key=dev_accs.get)
 195:             dev_fixed = float(dev_accs[dev_fixed_m])
 196: 
 197:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 198:     strata = _strata(pop)
 199:     boots = np.empty(n_boot)
 200:     for b in range(n_boot):
 201:         idx = _resample(strata, n_t, rng)
 202:         # best-fixed must be re-selected per bootstrap draw (held-out principle)
 203:         accs_b = {i: _acc(Y[i, idx]) for i in range(Y.shape[0])}
 204:         boots[b] = (_acc(np.nanmax(Y[:, idx], axis=0)) - max(accs_b.values()))
 205:     lo, hi = np.percentile(boots, [2.5, 97.5])
 206:     if lo > 0:
 207:         state = SUPPORTED
 208:     elif hi <= 1e-12:
 209:         state = REFUTED      # CI excludes positive coverage (includes exact-zero headroom)
 210:     else:
 211:         state = INSUFFICIENT
 212:     bare_acc = _acc(Y[0]) if pop.has_bare else None
 213:     return {
 214:         "state": state,
 215:         "oracle_accuracy": round(oracle, 4),
 216:         "best_fixed_member": best_fixed_m, "best_fixed_accuracy": round(best_fixed, 4),
 217:         "dev_fixed_member": dev_fixed_m,
 218:         "dev_fixed_accuracy": None if dev_fixed is None else round(dev_fixed, 4),
 219:         "bare_accuracy": None if bare_acc is None else round(bare_acc, 4),
 220:         "headroom": round(headroom, 4),
 221:         "headroom_ci95": [round(lo, 4), round(hi, 4)],
 222:         "residual_coverage_vs_bare": None if bare_acc is None else round(oracle - bare_acc, 4),
 223:         "info_boundaries": ("oracle uses per-task outcomes of all members; best-fixed uses "
 224:                             "outcome-averages over the same eval tasks; dev-fixed uses dev "
 225:                             "data only; headroom is not a realizable gain (plan 2)"),
 226:     }

 228: 
 229: def _strata(pop: Population) -> dict:
 230:     groups: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
 231:     for j, t in enumerate(pop.tasks):
 232:         key = pop.task_meta.get(t, {}).get("stratum", "__all__")
 233:         groups.setdefault(str(key), []).append(j)
 234:     return groups
 235: 
 236: 
 237: def _resample(strata: dict, n_t: int, rng) -> np.ndarray:
 238:     parts = []
 239:     for _, idxs in strata.items():
 240:         idxs = np.asarray(idxs)
 241:         parts.append(rng.choice(idxs, len(idxs), replace=True))
 242:     return np.concatenate(parts)

 245: # --------------------------------------------------------- S3 same-condition repeats
 246: 
 247: def _missing_bounds_delta(y1: np.ndarray, y2: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float]:
 248:     """Worst/best-case pair delta under every imputation of unknown cells.
 249: 
 250:     Observed delta counts missing as not-correct (denominator-preserving). These
 251:     bounds report how much the *unknown* cells alone could move the delta, so a
 252:     difference is never read as identified when missingness could flip it.
 253:     """
 254:     t = len(y1)
 255:     lo = hi = 0.0
 256:     for a, b in zip(y1, y2):
 257:         a_vals = [0.0, 1.0] if np.isnan(a) else [float(a)]
 258:         b_vals = [0.0, 1.0] if np.isnan(b) else [float(b)]
 259:         diffs = [a - b for a in a_vals for b in b_vals]
 260:         lo += min(diffs)
 261:         hi += max(diffs)
 262:     return lo / t, hi / t
 263: 
 264: 
 265: def _canonical_pairs(member_ids: list[str]) -> list[tuple[int, int, str, str]]:
 266:     """Directional pairs keyed by member ID order, NOT list position.
 267: 
 268:     Reversing or permuting the member list must not flip a pair's direction:
 269:     h1 is always the lexicographically smaller member id, so the delta
 270:     acc(h1)-acc(h2) is a property of the named pair, not of the input ordering.
 271:     """
 272:     order = sorted(range(len(member_ids)), key=lambda i: member_ids[i])
 273:     pairs = []
 274:     for x in range(len(order)):
 275:         for y in range(x + 1, len(order)):
 276:             i, j = order[x], order[y]
 277:             pairs.append((i, j, member_ids[i], member_ids[j]))
 278:     return pairs

 281: def s3_stability(pop_by_condition: dict[str, Population]) -> dict:
 282:     """Plan 3.C (v2): matched same-condition repeats, two separated estimands.
 283: 
 284:     Estimand 1 (stable ranking): for a member pair, the same-condition accuracy
 285:     difference with task-level bootstrap CI, sign-consistent across repeats.
 286:     Population state SUPPORTED iff some canonical pair shows a stable
 287:     difference in either direction. Permutation invariance is structural:
 288:     pair direction is fixed by member ID, never by list position.
 289: 
 290:     Estimand 2 (stable complementarity / task-harness interaction):
 291:     H_stable = E_x max_h q_h(x) - max_h E_x q_h(x), where q_h(x) is member h's
 292:     expected correctness on task x estimated across repeats. H_stable = 0 iff
 293:     one fixed member is expectation-best on every task (global dominance), so
 294:     a stable ranking difference CANNOT substitute for complementarity.
 295: 
 296:     Identity gates (v2): repeats with differing `condition` fields, differing
 297:     per-member `source_hashes`, or exactly duplicated outcome matrices are
 298:     refused as matched repeats (explicit INSUFFICIENT, with the offending
 299:     fields listed) - mixing conditions or cloned matrices can never produce a
 300:     SUPPORTED/REFUTED stability claim.
 301:     """
 302:     conds = sorted(pop_by_condition)
 303:     abstain = lambda reason, extra=None: {
 304:         "state": INSUFFICIENT, "reason": reason,
 305:         "minimal_missing_evidence": [extra] if extra else []}
 306:     if len(conds) < MIN_REPEATS:
 307:         return abstain(
 308:             f"R={len(conds)} matched condition groups < {MIN_REPEATS}",
 309:             f"collect >= {MIN_REPEATS} same-condition repeats (all c fields equal) "
 310:             f"over >= {MIN_REPEAT_TASKS} shared tasks")
 311:     base = pop_by_condition[conds[0]]
 312:     for c in conds[1:]:
 313:         p = pop_by_condition[c]
 314:         if p.member_ids != base.member_ids or p.tasks != base.tasks:
 315:             return abstain("membership/task set differs across conditions",
 316:                            "matched membership and tasks across repeats")
 317:     # --- identity gate 1: execution condition fields must match exactly
 318:     cond_fields = sorted({k for c in conds for k in pop_by_condition[c].condition})
 319:     cond_mismatch = {}
 320:     for f in cond_fields:
 321:         vals = {str(pop_by_condition[c].condition.get(f)) for c in conds}
 322:         if len(vals) > 1:
 323:             cond_mismatch[f] = sorted(vals)
 324:     if cond_mismatch:
 325:         return abstain(
 326:             "execution condition fields differ across purported repeats; "
 327:             "these are different conditions, not matched repeats",
 328:             "collect repeats under one identical execution condition")
 329:     # --- identity gate 2: member source identity must be constant across repeats
 330:     identity_conflicts = []
 331:     for i, m in enumerate(base.member_ids):
 332:         hashes = {pop_by_condition[c].source_hashes[i] for c in conds}
 333:         if len(hashes) > 1:
 334:             identity_conflicts.append({"member": m, "hashes": sorted(hashes)})
 335:     if identity_conflicts:
 336:         return abstain(
 337:             "member source identity differs across repeats (changed code "
 338:             "masquerading as same-condition repeats)",
 339:             "re-collect repeats under frozen member source code")
 340:     # --- identity gate 3: duplicated matrices are not independent executions
 341:     identical_pairs = []
 342:     for a in range(len(conds)):
 343:         for b in range(a + 1, len(conds)):
 344:             Ya, Yb = pop_by_condition[conds[a]].Y, pop_by_condition[conds[b]].Y
 345:             if Ya.shape == Yb.shape and np.array_equal(Ya, Yb, equal_nan=True):
 346:                 identical_pairs.append([conds[a], conds[b]])
 347:     if identical_pairs:
 348:         return abstain(
 349:             "repeats contain exactly identical outcome matrices; independence "
 350:             "of executions cannot be verified",
 351:             "re-run repeats as separate executions (or bind provenance showing "
 352:             "independence)")
 353:     Y = np.stack([pop_by_condition[c].Y for c in conds])       # (R, members, tasks)
 354:     R, M, T = Y.shape
 355:     if T < MIN_REPEAT_TASKS:
 356:         return abstain(f"T={T} shared tasks < {MIN_REPEAT_TASKS}",
 357:                        f">= {MIN_REPEAT_TASKS} shared tasks per repeat")
 358:     rng = np.random.default_rng(20260915)
 359:     pair_reports = []
 360:     stable_diff_exists = False
 361:     decisive_nonconsistent = False
 362:     for i, j, id1, id2 in _canonical_pairs(base.member_ids):
 363:         deltas = [_acc(Y[r, i]) - _acc(Y[r, j]) for r in range(R)]
 364:         boots = []
 365:         for _ in range(2000):
 366:             idx = rng.choice(T, T, replace=True)
 367:             boots.append(np.nansum(Y[:, i, idx], axis=1) / T
 368:                          - np.nansum(Y[:, j, idx], axis=1) / T)
 369:         lo_all, hi_all = np.percentile(np.mean(boots, axis=1), [2.5, 97.5])
 370:         signs = {int(np.sign(d)) for d in deltas}
 371:         if lo_all > 0 and signs == {1}:
 372:             st = SUPPORTED
 373:         elif hi_all < 0 and signs == {-1}:
 374:             st = REFUTED        # stable difference, direction opposite canonical
 375:         else:
 376:             st = INSUFFICIENT
 377:             if hi_all < 0 or lo_all > 0:
 378:                 decisive_nonconsistent = True
 379:         if st in (SUPPORTED, REFUTED):
 380:             stable_diff_exists = True
 381:         mlo, mhi = _missing_bounds_delta(_nanmean(Y[:, i, :], 0),
 382:                                          _nanmean(Y[:, j, :], 0))
 383:         pair_reports.append({
 384:             "h1": id1, "h2": id2, "state": st,
 385:             "mean_delta": round(float(np.mean(deltas)), 4),
 386:             "ci95": [round(float(lo_all), 4), round(float(hi_all), 4)],
 387:             "missing_sensitivity_bounds": [round(mlo, 4), round(mhi, 4)],
 388:             "direction_note": "h1/h2 fixed by member id order; independent of "
 389:                               "input member ordering"})
 390:     if stable_diff_exists:
 391:         rank_state = SUPPORTED
 392:     elif decisive_nonconsistent:
 393:         rank_state = REFUTED
 394:     else:
 395:         rank_state = INSUFFICIENT
 396: 
 397:     # --- Estimand 2: stable complementarity H_stable on repeat-averaged q_h(x)
 398:     with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
 399:         Q = _nanmean(Y, axis=0)                     # (members, tasks) q estimates
 400:     q_filled = np.where(np.isnan(Q), 0.0, Q)
 401:     per_task_max = q_filled.max(axis=0)
 402:     best_fixed_idx = int(np.argmax(q_filled.mean(axis=1)))
 403:     h_stable = float(per_task_max.mean() - q_filled[best_fixed_idx].mean())
 404:     boots_h = []
 405:     rng_h = np.random.default_rng(20260915)
 406:     for _ in range(2000):
 407:         idx = rng_h.choice(T, T, replace=True)
 408:         boots_h.append(per_task_max[idx].mean() - q_filled[best_fixed_idx, idx].mean())
 409:     lo_h, hi_h = np.percentile(boots_h, [2.5, 97.5])
 410:     if lo_h > 0:
 411:         comp_state = SUPPORTED
 412:     elif hi_h <= 1e-12:
 413:         comp_state = REFUTED      # consistent with a single expectation-best member
 414:     else:
 415:         comp_state = INSUFFICIENT
 416:     return {
 417:         "state": rank_state,
 418:         "R": R, "shared_tasks": T,
 419:         "condition_fields_verified": cond_fields,
 420:         "identity_checks": {"condition_mismatch": {}, "identity_conflicts": [],
 421:                             "identical_repeat_pairs": []},
 422:         "estimand": {
 423:             "stable_ranking": "pairwise same-condition accuracy difference (canonical "
 424:                               "member-id direction); SUPPORTED iff some pair is stable "
 425:                               "in either direction; permutation invariant by construction",
 426:             "stable_complementarity": "H_stable = E_x max_h q_h(x) - max_h E_x q_h(x); "
 427:                                       "zero iff one member is expectation-best on all "
 428:                                       "tasks; ranking differences do not imply this",
 429:         },
 430:         "stable_ranking": {"state": rank_state, "pairs": pair_reports},
 431:         "stable_complementarity": {
 432:             "state": comp_state, "H_stable": round(h_stable, 4),
 433:             "H_ci95": [round(float(lo_h), 4), round(float(hi_h), 4)],
 434:             "expectation_best_member": base.member_ids[best_fixed_idx],
 435:             "caveat": "q_h(x) estimated from R repeats; E[max] of noisy estimates is "
 436:                       "biased upward, so SUPPORTED near zero should be treated with "
 437:                       "the CI and repeat count in mind"},
 438:         "note": ("pairing is across same-condition repeats; cross-time/provider batches "
 439:                  "are non_exchangeable and excluded from this estimate"),
 440:     }
 441: 
 442: 
 443: # ------------------------------------------------------ S4 pre-execution selectability
 444: 
 445: def _softmax(z):
 446:     z = z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
 447:     e = np.exp(z)
 448:     return e / e.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
 449: 
 450: 
 451: def _sigmoid(z):
 452:     return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(z, -30, 30)))
 453: 
 454: 
 455: def _fit_member_probs(X_dev, Y_dev, X_ev, epochs=2000, lr=0.5):
 456:     """Frozen policy core: per-member logistic P(Y_h=1 | features), fit on dev.
 457: 
 458:     Tie-free alternative to argmax labelling; returns predicted per-member
 459:     correct probabilities on eval rows (n_ev, n_members).
 460:     """
 461:     n_m = Y_dev.shape[0]
 462:     probs = np.zeros((X_ev.shape[0], n_m))
 463:     for h in range(n_m):
 464:         y = Y_dev[h]
 465:         if np.all(np.isnan(y)):
 466:             continue
 467:         w = np.zeros(X_dev.shape[1])
 468:         b0 = float(np.log(np.clip(np.nanmean(y), 1e-3, 0.999)) *
 469:                    -np.log(1 - np.clip(np.nanmean(y), 1e-3, 0.999)))
 470:         b0 = 0.0
 471:         valid = ~np.isnan(y)
 472:         for _ in range(epochs):
 473:             p = _sigmoid(X_dev[valid] @ w + b0)
 474:             g = (X_dev[valid].T @ (p - y[valid])) / max(1, valid.sum())
 475:             w -= lr * g
 476:             b0 -= lr * float(np.mean(p - y[valid]))
 477:         probs[:, h] = _sigmoid(X_ev @ w + b0)
 478:     return probs
 479: 
 480: 
 481: def _feature_matrix(pop: Population, idxs: list[int]) -> np.ndarray:
 482:     strata = sorted(_strata(pop))
 483:     X = np.zeros((len(idxs), len(strata) + 1))
 484:     for r, j in enumerate(idxs):
 485:         key = str(pop.task_meta.get(pop.tasks[j], {}).get("stratum", "__all__"))
 486:         X[r, strata.index(key) if key in strata else len(strata)] = 1.0
 487:     return X
 488: 
 489: 
 490: def _policy_choices(pop: Population, dev_idx: list[int], ev_idx: list[int]) -> np.ndarray:
 491:     """Frozen pi_Z: argmax_h P_h(correct|Z(x)); abstain->bare when top-2 gap <
 492:     ABSTAIN_EPS. (Calibration removed the dev-accuracy log prior: it swamped
 493:     stratum-level signals and duplicated dev-fixed selection; frozen for blinded.)"""
 494:     X_dev = _feature_matrix(pop, dev_idx)
 495:     X_ev = _feature_matrix(pop, ev_idx)
 496:     probs = _fit_member_probs(X_dev, pop.Y[:, dev_idx], X_ev)
 497:     top2 = np.sort(probs, axis=1)[:, -2:]
 498:     return np.where((top2[:, 1] - top2[:, 0]) < ABSTAIN_EPS, 0, np.argmax(probs, axis=1))
 499: 
 500: 
 501: def s4_selectability(pop: Population, seed: int = 20260915) -> dict:
 502:     """Plan 3.D: frozen pi_Z vs dev-fixed on held-out eval tasks.
 503: 
 504:     Features per task: one-hot task stratum (database/subject) + pre-execution
 505:     metadata; member prior from dev accuracies is a bias term only. Training uses
 506:     dev tasks exclusively. Abstain -> bare when top-2 posterior gap < ABSTAIN_EPS.
 507:     """
 508:     if not pop.dev_task_ids:
 509:         return {"state": INSUFFICIENT,
 510:                 "reason": "no development split available for frozen policy training",
 511:                 "minimal_missing_evidence": ["a dev split disjoint from eval tasks"]}
 512:     dev_idx = [pop.tasks.index(t) for t in pop.dev_task_ids if t in pop.tasks]
 513:     ev_idx = [j for j, t in enumerate(pop.tasks) if t not in set(pop.dev_task_ids)]
 514:     if not ev_idx:
 515:         return {"state": INSUFFICIENT, "reason": "no held-out eval tasks"}
 516: 
 517:     strata = sorted(_strata(pop))
 518:     def feats(idxs):
 519:         return _feature_matrix(pop, idxs)
 520: 
 521:     # class prior from dev (member-level pre-execution info), applied as bias
 522:     dev_acc = _accs_rows(pop.Y[:, dev_idx])
 523: 
 524:     choice = _policy_choices(pop, dev_idx, ev_idx)
 525: 
 526:     Y_ev = pop.Y[:, ev_idx]
 527:     pi_acc = np.array([Y_ev[c, j] for j, c in enumerate(choice)])
 528:     valid = ~np.isnan(pi_acc)
 529:     pi_rate = float(np.nansum(pi_acc) / len(pi_acc))
 530:     dev_fixed_idx = int(np.argmax(_accs_rows(pop.Y[:, dev_idx])))
 531:     paired = pi_acc - Y_ev[dev_fixed_idx]
 532:     n_valid = int(valid.sum())
 533:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 534:     # denominator-preserving: unknown cells count as 0, stay in the denominator
 535:     boots = [float(np.nansum(rng.choice(paired, len(paired), replace=True))) / len(paired) for _ in range(4000)]
 536:     lo, hi = np.percentile(boots, [2.5, 97.5])
 537:     if lo > 0:
 538:         state = SUPPORTED
 539:     elif hi < 0:
 540:         state = REFUTED
 541:     else:
 542:         state = INSUFFICIENT
 543:     return {
 544:         "state": state,
 545:         "policy": "frozen multinomial LR on task stratum one-hot + dev-accuracy prior; "
 546:                   f"abstain->bare when top-2 gap < {ABSTAIN_EPS}",
 547:         "eval_tasks": len(ev_idx), "abstain_rate": round(float((choice == 0).mean()), 4),
 548:         "pi_Z_accuracy": round(pi_rate, 4),
 549:         "dev_fixed_member": pop.member_ids[dev_fixed_idx],
 550:         "dev_fixed_accuracy": round(_acc(Y_ev[dev_fixed_idx]), 4),
 551:         "pi_Z_minus_devfixed_ci95": [round(lo, 4), round(hi, 4)],
 552:         "leakage_boundary": "training used dev tasks only; eval tasks never entered fitting",
 553:     }
 554: 
 555: 
 556: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ S5 cost model
 557: 
 558: def s5_cost(pop: Population, s4: dict) -> dict:
 559:     """Plan 3.E: P = pi_Z single-member (1 call/task) vs dev-fixed (1 call/task).
 560: 
 561:     Cost-matched by construction; oracle-routing (K calls) is a post-execution
 562:     reference only. Net utility U = acc diff - LAMBDA_HARM * harm diff; harm =
 563:     wrong while bare right. Missing call counts force INSUFFICIENT for claims
 564:     beyond the matched-budget design.
 565:     """
 566:     if not pop.has_bare or s4.get("state") in (INSUFFICIENT,) and "dev split" in s4.get("reason", ""):
 567:         return {"state": INSUFFICIENT, "reason": "pi_Z unavailable or no bare reference",
 568:                 "minimal_missing_evidence": ["trainable dev split"]}
 569:     if not pop.calls:
 570:         # Distinguish "no evidence supplied by this adapter/caller" from
 571:         # "the archive contains no call records" - never conflate the two.
 572:         cost_evidence = {"status": pop.calls_status if pop.calls_status != "not_provided"
 573:                          else "calls_not_provided",
 574:                          "note": "absence of a populated calls dict is NOT evidence "
 575:                                  "that the archive lacks call records"}
 576:     else:
 577:         per_call = [v for v in pop.calls.values() if v is not None]
 578:         cost_evidence = {"status": pop.calls_status if pop.calls_status != "not_provided"
 579:                          else "per_record",
 580:                          "median_calls": float(np.median(per_call)) if per_call else None}
 581:     # U is computed on the same eval tasks as S4 by re-running the frozen choice rule
 582:     dev_idx = [pop.tasks.index(t) for t in pop.dev_task_ids if t in pop.tasks]
 583:     ev_idx = [j for j, t in enumerate(pop.tasks) if t not in set(pop.dev_task_ids)]
 584:     if not ev_idx:
 585:         return {"state": INSUFFICIENT, "reason": "no held-out eval tasks"}
 586:     choice = _policy_choices(pop, dev_idx, ev_idx)
 587:     Y_ev = pop.Y[:, ev_idx]
 588:     pi_acc = np.array([Y_ev[c, j] for j, c in enumerate(choice)])
 589:     dev_fixed_idx = int(np.argmax(_accs_rows(pop.Y[:, dev_idx])))
 590:     bare = Y_ev[0]
 591:     harm_P = float(np.mean((pi_acc == 0) & (bare == 1)))
 592:     harm_D = float(np.mean((Y_ev[dev_fixed_idx] == 0) & (bare == 1)))
 593:     U = float(np.nansum(pi_acc) / len(pi_acc) - _acc(Y_ev[dev_fixed_idx]) - LAMBDA_HARM * (harm_P - harm_D))
 594:     paired = (pi_acc - Y_ev[dev_fixed_idx]) - LAMBDA_HARM * (
 595:         ((pi_acc == 0) & (bare == 1)).astype(float) - ((Y_ev[dev_fixed_idx] == 0) & (bare == 1)).astype(float))
 596:     rng = np.random.default_rng(20260915)
 597:     boots = [np.nansum(rng.choice(paired, len(paired), replace=True)) / len(paired) for _ in range(4000)]
 598:     lo, hi = np.percentile(boots, [2.5, 97.5])
 599:     state = SUPPORTED if lo > 0 else (REFUTED if hi < 0 else INSUFFICIENT)
 600:     return {
 601:         "state": state, "policy": "pi_Z single member", "budget_calls_per_task": BUDGET_CALLS,
 602:         "lambda_harm": LAMBDA_HARM, "comparator": "dev-fixed (same budget)",
 603:         "U": round(U, 4), "U_ci95": [round(lo, 4), round(hi, 4)],
 604:         "cost_evidence": cost_evidence,
 605:         "note": ("real dollar/token costs are not recoverable from these archives; SUPPORT "
 606:                  "is limited to the matched 1-call budget, not billable deployment"),
 607:     }
 608: 
 609: 
 610: def assemble_report(s1: dict, s2: dict, s3: dict, s4: dict, s5: dict) -> dict:
 611:     return {
 612:         "A_measurement_sufficiency": s1,
 613:         "B_single_shot_coverage": s2,
 614:         "C_stability": s3,
 615:         "D_pre_execution_selectability": s4,
 616:         "E_policy_utility": s5,
 617:         "state_vocabulary": [SUPPORTED, REFUTED, INSUFFICIENT, NOT_APPLICABLE],
 618:         "states_are_project_definitions": True,
 619:     }

  56:     pop, counters, v2_rows = load_population(manifest, dev_ids)
  57:     # remove dev tasks from the eval matrix for D/E/B claims
  58:     ev_idx = [j for j, t in enumerate(pop.tasks) if t not in set(dev_ids)]
  59:     pop_eval = core.Population(
  60:         member_ids=pop.member_ids, source_hashes=pop.source_hashes,

  62:         condition=pop.condition, has_bare=True, dev_task_ids=dev_ids,

  65:     s1 = core.s1_integrity(manifest, pop, counters["judge_replay_mismatches"],

 161: def _run_diagnostic(pop) -> dict:
 162:     """Run S1-S5 on a Population, or on {repeat_key: Population} for
 163:     repeat-based controls (S3 then evaluates the matched-repeat estimands)."""
 164:     if isinstance(pop, dict):
 165:         base = pop[sorted(pop)[0]]
 166:         repeats = pop
 167:     else:
 168:         base = pop
 169:         repeats = None
 170:     manifest_mock = {"member_ids": base.member_ids, "task_ids": base.tasks}
 171:     s1 = core.s1_integrity(manifest_mock, base, base.judge_replay_mismatches,
 172:                            base.duplicate_keys, [])
 173:     s2 = core.s2_decomposition(base)
 174:     s3 = (core.s3_stability(repeats) if repeats is not None
 175:           else _s3_for_pop(base))
 176:     s4 = core.s4_selectability(base)
 177:     s5 = core.s5_cost(base, s4)
 178:     return {"A": s1["state"], "B": s2["state"], "C": s3["state"],
 179:             "C_comp": s3.get("stable_complementarity", {}).get("state", INSUFFICIENT),
 180:             "D": s4["state"], "E": s5["state"],
 181:             "detail": {"A": s1, "B": s2, "C": s3, "D": s4, "E": s5}}

 184: def _m0_metrics(pop: core.Population) -> dict:
 185:     """Traditional single-shot population metrics only (mean member acc, oracle).
 186: 
 187:     Comparison reference only; still denominator-preserving on missing cells."""
 188:     Y = pop.Y
 189:     return {"mean_member_accuracy": round(float(np.nansum(Y) / Y.size), 4),
 190:             "oracle_accuracy": round(float(np.nansum(np.nanmax(Y, axis=0)) / Y.shape[1]), 4)}

 193: def _m1_metrics(pop: core.Population) -> dict:
 194:     """Competent decomposition baseline + basic integrity checks."""
 195:     Y = pop.Y
 196:     dup_cols = len(pop.tasks) - len(set(pop.tasks))
 197:     return {**_m0_metrics(pop),
 198:             "best_fixed": round(float((np.nansum(Y, axis=1) / Y.shape[1]).max()), 4),
 199:             "headroom": round(float(np.nansum(np.nanmax(Y, axis=0)) / Y.shape[1]
 200:                                     - (np.nansum(Y, axis=1) / Y.shape[1]).max()), 4),
 201:             "integrity": {"duplicate_task_ids": dup_cols,
 202:                           "missing_cells": int(np.isnan(Y).sum())}}

 205: def run_controls(phase: str, out: Path) -> dict:
 206:     package = ctl.build_package()
 207:     challenge_results = None
 208:     if phase == "blinded":
 209:         # Challenges are RE-EXECUTED from the frozen spec under the current code
 210:         # (bound to spec + code hashes). A missing spec is a hard block, not a
 211:         # silent skip: the blinded set is undefined without the pre-committed
 212:         # challenges.
 213:         if not chal.SPEC_PATH.exists():
 214:             raise FileNotFoundError(
 215:                 f"challenge spec missing: {chal.SPEC_PATH} - blinded validation "
 216:                 "cannot run without the pre-committed challenges")
 217:         spec_sha = chal.spec_sha256()
 218:         expected_sha = None
 219:         sha_file = chal.SPEC_PATH.with_suffix(".sha256")
 220:         if sha_file.exists():
 221:             expected_sha = sha_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip().split()[0]
 222:         if expected_sha and spec_sha != expected_sha:
 223:             raise ValueError(
 224:                 f"challenge spec hash mismatch: {spec_sha} != recorded {expected_sha}")
 225:         challenge_results = chal.execute_challenges(_run_diagnostic)
 226:         package["challenges_executed"] = {
 227:             "spec_sha256": spec_sha, "code_sha256": challenge_results["code_sha256"]}
 228:         package["blinded"] = package["blinded"] + list(challenge_results["challenges"])
 229:     (out / f"control_manifest_{phase}.json").write_text(
 230:         json.dumps(package, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
 231:     classes = ("A", "B", "C", "C_comp", "D", "E")
 232:     rows = []
 233:     for c in package["controls"]:
 234:         if c["instance_phase"] != phase:
 235:             continue
 236:         pop = ctl.get_control(c["cid"], c["instance"])
 237:         got = _run_diagnostic(pop)
 238:         exp = c["expected"]
 239:         verdict = {k: "OK" if got[k] == exp[k] else "WRONG" for k in classes}
 240:         rows.append({"control": f"{c['cid']}#{c['instance']}",
 241:                      "description": c["description"], "expected": exp,
 242:                      "got": {k: got[k] for k in classes},
 243:                      "verdict": verdict})
 244:     if phase == "blinded":
 245:         for cid, r in challenge_results["challenges"].items():
 246:             rows.append({"control": cid,
 247:                          "description": "auditor challenge RE-EXECUTED from spec "
 248:                                         "under current code (hash-bound)",
 249:                          "expected": r["expected"],
 250:                          "got": r["got"],
 251:                          "verdict": {k: ("OK" if r["got"][k] == r["expected"][k]
 252:                                          else "WRONG") for k in r["expected"]}})
 253:     n = len(rows)
 254:     wrong = sum(1 for r in rows if "WRONG" in r["verdict"].values())
 255:     cells = [(r, k) for r in rows for k in r["expected"]]
 256:     n_nonsup = sum(1 for r, k in cells if r["expected"][k] != SUPPORTED)
 257:     false_support = sum(1 for r, k in cells
 258:                         if r["got"][k] == SUPPORTED and r["expected"][k] != SUPPORTED)
 259:     n_clear = sum(1 for r, k in cells
 260:                   if r["expected"][k] in (SUPPORTED, REFUTED))
 261:     wrongful_abstain = sum(1 for r, k in cells
 262:                            if r["got"][k] == INSUFFICIENT
 263:                            and r["expected"][k] in (SUPPORTED, REFUTED))
 264:     metrics = {
 265:         "n_controls": n, "n_any_wrong": wrong,
 266:         "N_nonSUPPORTED": n_nonsup, "N_clear": n_clear,
 267:         "false_support_rate": round(false_support / max(1, n_nonsup), 4),
 268:         "false_support_pass": false_support / max(1, n_nonsup) <= 0.1,
 269:         "wrongful_abstain": wrongful_abstain,
 270:         "abstain_cap_pass": wrongful_abstain <= max(3, int(0.3 * n_clear)),
 271:         "abstain_rate_all_cells": round(sum(1 for r, k in cells
 272:                                             if r["got"][k] == INSUFFICIENT)
 273:                                         / max(1, len(cells)), 4),
 274:         "positive_control_recognized": all(
 275:             r["verdict"][k] == "OK" for r in rows
 276:             if r["control"].startswith("C4") for k in ("D", "E")),
 277:     }
 278:     result = {"phase": phase, "metrics": metrics, "rows": rows,
 279:               "thresholds": {"false_support_rate_max": 0.1,
 280:                              "abstain_cap": "3 or 30% of N_clear"},
 281:               "challenge_execution": (
 282:                   challenge_results if challenge_results else
 283:                   "not applicable (calibration phase)"),
 284:               "m0_example": _m0_metrics(ctl.get_control("C4", 1)),
 285:               "m1_example": _m1_metrics(ctl.get_control("C4", 1)),
 286:               "note": "M0/M1 are reported as comparison references; the full method "
 287:                       "comparison table is assembled in CONTROL_VALIDATION.json"}
 288:     (out / f"control_validation_{phase}.json").write_text(
 289:         json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
 290:     return result

 293: def verify_challenges(out: Path, result_path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
 294:     """HISTORICAL REPLAY ONLY: verify a stored challenge result file against the
 295:     spec hash it records, without treating it as validation of the current code.
 296: 
 297:     Current-code validation lives in `controls --phase blinded`, which
 298:     re-executes the challenges. This command exists so the archived auditor
 299:     result keeps its provenance while never being conflated with a fresh pass.
 300:     """
 301:     if result_path is None:
 302:         raise SystemExit(
 303:             "verify-challenges requires --challenge-result PATH (no directory "
 304:             "scanning: the newest file must never be silently selected)")
 305:     stored = json.loads(result_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 306:     spec_sha_now = chal.spec_sha256()
 307:     spec_sha_stored = stored.get("challenge_spec_sha256")
 308:     report = {
 309:         "result_path": str(result_path),
 310:         "stored_spec_sha256": spec_sha_stored,
 311:         "current_spec_sha256": spec_sha_now,
 312:         "spec_hash_matches": spec_sha_stored == spec_sha_now,
 313:         "code_binding_of_stored_result": stored.get("code_sha256"),
 314:         "status": "HISTORICAL_REPLAY",
 315:         "note": ("verification of what the stored run concluded at its time; "
 316:                  "NOT evidence that the current diagnostics code passes the "
 317:                  "challenges - see controls --phase blinded"),
 318:     }
 319:     if spec_sha_stored != spec_sha_now:
 320:         report["discrepancy"] = (
 321:             "the stored result was produced under a different spec binding; per "
 322:             "the 2026-09-15 review, its CH2 numbers are also inconsistent with "
 323:             "the spec's generating rule (best_fixed 0.94 is unreachable; the "
 324:             "spec forces 0.79). The stored file is retained for provenance only.")
 325:     (out / "challenge_historical_replay.json").write_text(
 326:         json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
 327:     return report

 330: def inventory(out: Path) -> dict:
 331:     """Full archive inventory rows (plan 6): every member x task pair, staged."""
 332:     manifest = build_manifest()
 333:     pop, counters, _ = load_population(manifest)

 339:                          "state": "included" if not np.isnan(v) else "missing",
 340:                          "verdict": None if np.isnan(v) else int(v)})
 341:     data = load_bird()

 343:         for i, h in enumerate(p.member_ids):

 347:                              "task": t,
 348:                              "state": "included" if not np.isnan(v) else "missing",
 349:                              "verdict": None if np.isnan(v) else int(v)})
 350:     with (out / "ARCHIVE_INVENTORY.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
 351:         w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["archive", "member", "task", "state", "verdict"])
 352:         w.writeheader()

 354:     counts = {}
 355:     for r in rows:
 356:         counts[r["archive"]] = counts.get(r["archive"], 0) + 1
 357:     return {"n_rows": len(rows), "by_archive": counts}

1: """BIRD (phase2) archive adapter: thin wrapper over the canonical replay loader.
   2: 
   3: Reuses experiment.revision.replay (manifest-verified, duplicate-aware) instead of
   4: reimplementing loading. Produces per-(builder, seed) x arm Populations. All
   5: historical primary rows are repeat 0 / cache on -> S3 abstains by the frozen rule.
   6: """
   7: from __future__ import annotations
   8: 
   9: import sys
  10: from pathlib import Path
  11: 
  12: import numpy as np
  13: 
  14: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
  15: sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
  16: 
  17: from experiment.revision import replay as rp  # noqa: E402
  18: from experiment.diagnostics.core import Population  # noqa: E402
  19: 
  20: 
  21: def load_bird() -> dict:
  22:     """Return {cell_key: {arm: Population}} plus shared task/bare info."""
  23:     manifests = {
  24:         "AD": ROOT / "artifacts/phase2/primary_input_manifest.json",
  25:         "BC": ROOT / "artifacts/phase2/bc_input_manifest.json",
  26:     }
  27:     groups, _inventory, audit = rp.load_sources(manifests)
  28:     mem, _files, generation = rp.membership()
  29:     # BC collections cover the stratified 400-task CORE subsample; AD covers the
  30:     # full 1169-task test split. Use the core intersection so every arm's rows
  31:     # exist; AD-bare rows outside the core are simply not selected.
  32:     split_path = ROOT / "experiment/phase2" / "split_p2_test_core.json"
  33:     tasks = rp.task_ids(split_path)
  34:     # restrict to tasks present in BOTH collections (bare source = AD)
  35:     def has_all(rows, hs):
  36:         return all((rp.TARGET, h, t, 0, False) in rows for t in tasks for h in hs)
  37:     ad_rows = groups["AD"]
  38:     tasks = [t for t in tasks if (rp.TARGET, "bare", t, 0, False) in ad_rows]
  39:     dbs = {}
  40:     for tk in tasks:
  41:         db = tk.split("#")[0]
  42:         dbs[tk] = {"stratum": db}
  43:     bare_vec = rp.vector(groups["AD"], "bare", tasks)
  44:     out = {}
  45:     logical_calls_total = 0
  46:     calls_rows_seen = 0
  47:     for (builder, seed) in sorted({(b, s) for b, s, _ in mem}):
  48:         for arm in "ABCD":
  49:             names = mem[(builder, seed, arm)]
  50:             rows = groups["AD" if arm in "AD" else "BC"]
  51:             members = ["bare"] + names
  52:             Y = np.vstack([bare_vec] + [rp.vector(rows, h, tasks) for h in names])
  53:             hashes = []
  54:             for h in members:
  55:                 hs = {r["code_hash"] for (tg, hh, *_), r in rows.items() if hh == h}
  56:                 hashes.append(sorted(hs)[0] if len(hs) == 1 else "CONFLICT:" + ",".join(sorted(hs)))
  57:             # per-record logical calls ARE archived (n_llm_calls); read them here
  58:             # instead of reporting "no cost data" (review P0: recorded-but-unread
  59:             # must not be conflated with not-recorded)
  60:             calls = {}
  61:             for h in members:
  62:                 for tk in tasks:
  63:                     r = rows.get((rp.TARGET, h, tk, 0, False))
  64:                     if r is not None and r.get("n_llm_calls") is not None:
  65:                         calls[(h, tk)] = r["n_llm_calls"]
  66:             logical_calls_total += sum(calls.values())
  67:             calls_rows_seen += len(calls)
  68:             out[(builder, seed, arm)] = Population(
  69:                 member_ids=members, source_hashes=hashes, tasks=tasks, Y=Y,
  70:                 condition={"target": rp.TARGET, "repeat": 0, "no_cache": False},
  71:                 has_bare=True, dev_task_ids=[], task_meta=dbs, calls=calls,
  72:                 calls_status="per_record")
  73:     return {"cells": out, "tasks": tasks, "audit": audit, "generation": generation,
  74:             "logical_calls_total": logical_calls_total,
  75:             "calls_rows_seen": calls_rows_seen}

1: """MATH-500 archive adapter for the diagnostics pipeline.  13: from pathlib import Path
  14: 
  15: import numpy as np
  16: 
  17: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
  18: sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
  19: 
  20: from experiment.gsm8k.collect import _norm_latex, _to_float, extract_answer  # noqa: E402
  21: from experiment.diagnostics.core import Population, digest_file  # noqa: E402
  22: 
  23: ARCHIVE = ROOT / "artifacts/gsm8k_audit"
  24: RUN_FILES = ["run_math500.jsonl", "run_bare_math500.jsonl"]
  25: SPLIT = ARCHIVE / "math500_split.json"
  26: N_EVAL = 400
  27: 
  28: 
  29: def judge_v2(pred_text: str, gold: str) -> int:
  30:     """Endpoint/bracket-sensitive judge: identical to v1 except that bracketed
  31:     list answers keep their bracket context (recovered from the raw prediction
  32:     when extraction strips it) and two-element comparisons require matching
  33:     open/closed endpoints; >2-element bracketed lists (coordinate tuples) ignore
  34:     brackets."""
  35:     p = extract_answer(pred_text)
  36:     if p is None:
  37:         return 0
  38:     pf, gf = _to_float(p), _to_float(gold)
  39:     if pf is not None and gf is not None:
  40:         return int(pf == gf)
  41:     np_, ng = _norm_latex(p), _norm_latex(gold)
  42: 
  43:     def parse(s: str):
  44:         m = re.fullmatch(r"([\(\[])(.+)([\)\]])", s)
  45:         if not m:
  46:             return None
  47:         return m.group(1), m.group(2).split(","), m.group(3)
  48: 
  49:     # recover bracket context from the RAW prediction / RAW gold strings as a
  50:     # structured list; _norm_latex strips commas (digit-group heuristic) which
  51:     # would collapse "0,1" into one element and erase the endpoint distinction
  52:     def recover_struct(raw: str, extracted_norm: str):
  53:         stripped = re.sub(r"[\s$]", "", str(raw))
  54:         for tok in ("\\left", "\\right", "\\!"):
  55:             stripped = stripped.replace(tok, "")
  56:         for m in re.finditer(r"([\(\[])([^()\[\]]*)([\)\]])", stripped):
  57:             parts = m.group(2).split(",")
  58:             joined = "".join(_norm_latex(x) for x in parts)
  59:             if joined == extracted_norm:
  60:                 return m.group(1), parts, m.group(3)
  61:         return None
  62: 
  63:     rec_p = recover_struct(pred_text, _norm_latex(p))
  64:     rec_g = recover_struct(gold, _norm_latex(gold))
  65:     if rec_p and rec_g:
  66:         lb1, p1, rb1 = rec_p
  67:         lb2, p2, rb2 = rec_g
  68:         if len(p1) != len(p2):
  69:             return 0
  70:         if not all(_norm_latex(a) == _norm_latex(b) for a, b in zip(p1, p2)):
  71:             return 0
  72:         if len(p1) == 2:
  73:             return int(lb1 == lb2 and rb1 == rb2)
  74:         return 1
  75:     if rec_p or rec_g:
  76:         # only one side is a bracketed list -> fall back to normalized strings
  77:         np_ = f"{rec_p[0]}{','.join(rec_p[1])}{rec_p[2]}" if rec_p else np_
  78:         ng = f"{rec_g[0]}{','.join(rec_g[1])}{rec_g[2]}" if rec_g else ng
  79:         return int(_norm_latex(np_) == _norm_latex(ng) or np_ == ng)
  80:     if np_ == ng:
  81:         return 1
  82:     A, B = parse(np_), parse(ng)
  83:     if A and B:
  84:         lb1, p1, rb1 = A
  85:         lb2, p2, rb2 = B
  86:         if len(p1) != len(p2):
  87:             return 0
  88:         if not all(_norm_latex(a) == _norm_latex(b) for a, b in zip(p1, p2)):
  89:             return 0
  90:         if len(p1) == 2:
  91:             return int(lb1 == lb2 and rb1 == rb2)
  92:         return 1
  93:     return 0
  94: 
  95: 
  96: def build_manifest() -> dict:
  97:     """Freeze the explicit input manifest (members, tasks, file hashes)."""
  98:     split = json.loads(SPLIT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
  99:     eval_tasks = split["tasks"][100:]
 100:     task_ids = [f"math500_split#{i}" for i in range(100, 500)]
 101:     gold_by_tid = {task_ids[i]: eval_tasks[i]["gold"] for i in range(N_EVAL)}
 102:     members = set()
 103:     files = []
 104:     for fn in RUN_FILES:
 105:         p = ARCHIVE / fn
 106:         with p.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
 107:             for line in fh:
 108:                 if line.strip():
 109:                     members.add(json.loads(line)["harness_id"])
 110:         files.append({"file": fn, "sha256": digest_file(p)})
 111:     members = sorted(members)
 112:     meta = {tid: {"stratum": eval_tasks[i]["subject"]}
 113:             for i, tid in enumerate(task_ids)}
 114:     return {
 115:         "purpose": "MATH-500 archive diagnostics manifest (frozen)",
 116:         "archive": "artifacts/gsm8k_audit",
 117:         "files": files,
 118:         "member_ids": members,          # includes 'bare'
 119:         "task_ids": task_ids,
 120:         "dev_task_ids": [],             # dev = first 100, not run in this archive
 121:         "n_eval_tasks": N_EVAL,
 122:         "gold_by_tid": gold_by_tid,
 123:         "task_meta": meta,
 124:         "condition": {"target": "GLM-5.3-Flash", "repeat": 0, "no_cache": False,
 125:                       "judge": "experiment.gsm8k.collect.is_correct"},
 126:     }
 127: 
 128: 
 129: def load_population(manifest: dict, dev_task_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> tuple:
 130:     """Return (Population, s1_counters, v2_rescore_rows)."""
 131:     records: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
 132:     dup = conflicts = 0
 133:     for entry in manifest["files"]:
 134:         path = ARCHIVE / entry["file"]
 135:         if digest_file(path) != entry["sha256"]:
 136:             raise ValueError(f"manifest hash mismatch: {entry['file']}")
 137:         with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
 138:             for line_no, line in enumerate(fh, 1):
 139:                 if not line.strip():
 140:                     continue
 141:                 r = json.loads(line)
 142:                 key = (r["harness_id"], r["task_id"], r["repeat"], r["no_cache"])
 143:                 if key in records:
 144:                     dup += 1
 145:                     if records[key]["official_correct"] != r["official_correct"]:
 146:                         conflicts += 1
 147:                     continue
 148:                 records[key] = {**r, "source_line": line_no}
 149:     members = manifest["member_ids"]
 150:     tasks = manifest["task_ids"]
 151:     n, t = len(members), len(tasks)
 152:     midx = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(members)}
 153:     tidx = {tk: j for j, tk in enumerate(tasks)}
 154:     Y = np.full((n, t), np.nan)
 155:     calls: dict = {}
 156:     v2_rows = []
 157:     for (h, tid, rep, noc), r in records.items():
 158:         if rep != 0 or noc:
 159:             continue  # single-shot matrix = repeat 0, cache on
 160:         if h not in midx or tid not in tidx:
 161:             continue
 162:         gold = manifest["gold_by_tid"].get(tid)
 163:         if gold is None:
 164:             continue
 165:         i, j = midx[h], tidx[tid]
 166:         Y[i, j] = r["official_correct"]
 167:         if r.get("n_llm_calls") is not None:
 168:             calls[(h, tid)] = r["n_llm_calls"]
 169:         if "final_answer" in r:
 170:             v1 = int(r["official_correct"])
 171:             v2 = judge_v2(r.get("final_answer") or "", gold)
 172:             v2_rows.append({"harness_id": h, "task_id": tid,
 173:                             "v1": v1, "v2": v2,
 174:                             "final_answer": (r.get("final_answer") or "")[-2000:]})
 175:     # judge replay: v1 must reproduce archived verdicts (we already read them, so
 176:     # recompute independently to bind judge version to stored verdicts)
 177:     from experiment.gsm8k.collect import is_correct
 178:     judge_replay_mismatches = 0
 179:     for (h, tid, rep, noc), r in records.items():
 180:         if rep != 0 or noc:
 181:             continue
 182:         gold = manifest["gold_by_tid"].get(tid)
 183:         if gold is None or "final_answer" not in r:
 184:             continue
 185:         if is_correct(r["final_answer"], gold) != r["official_correct"]:
 186:             judge_replay_mismatches += 1
 187:     pop = Population(
 188:         member_ids=members,
 189:         source_hashes=["bare" if m == "bare" else f"sha:{m}" for m in members],
 190:         tasks=tasks, Y=Y,
 191:         condition=manifest["condition"], has_bare=True,
 192:         dev_task_ids=dev_task_ids or [],
 193:         task_meta=manifest["task_meta"], calls=calls,
 194:         calls_status="per_record" if calls else "absent_in_archive_rows")
 195:     return pop, {"duplicate_keys": dup, "verdict_conflicts": conflicts,
 196:                  "judge_replay_mismatches": judge_replay_mismatches}, v2_rows

 149: class TestS3Invariants(unittest.TestCase):
 150:     """Invariants the S3 stability estimands MUST satisfy (external review
 151:     2026-09-15): permutation invariance, dominance != complementarity, and
 152:     refusal of condition-mixed / cloned / identity-broken repeats."""
 153: 
 154:     @staticmethod
 155:     def _review_case(member_order):
 156:         """The reviewer's counterexample population: bare ~ Bernoulli(0.5)
 157:         independently per repeat, a right on the first 20 tasks, b right
 158:         everywhere - 40 tasks, 3 repeats. Only the MEMBER LIST ORDER varies;
 159:         the id->data mapping is fixed."""
 160:         data = {
 161:             "bare": (np.random.default_rng(900).random(40) < 0.5).astype(float),
 162:             "a":    np.concatenate([np.ones(20), np.zeros(20)]),
 163:             "b":    np.ones(40),
 164:         }
 165:         pops = {}
 166:         for r in range(3):
 167:             rows = []
 168:             for m in member_order:
 169:                 row = data[m].copy()
 170:                 if m == "bare":
 171:                     row = (np.random.default_rng(900 + r).random(40) < 0.5).astype(float)
 172:                 rows.append(row)
 173:             pops[f"r{r}"] = ctl.Population(
 174:                 member_ids=list(member_order),
 175:                 source_hashes=[f"h_{m}" for m in member_order],
 176:                 tasks=ctl._task_ids(40), Y=np.vstack(rows),
 177:                 condition={"c": "synthetic"}, has_bare=True,
 178:                 dev_task_ids=[], task_meta={}, calls={})
 179:         return pops
 180: 
 181:     def test_s3_population_conclusion_is_permutation_invariant(self):
 182:         s_ab = core.s3_stability(self._review_case(["bare", "a", "b"]))
 183:         s_ba = core.s3_stability(self._review_case(["bare", "b", "a"]))
 184:         # the pre-fix code returned REFUTED for one order and SUPPORTED for the
 185:         # other; the population-level conclusion must not depend on ordering
 186:         self.assertEqual(s_ab["state"], s_ba["state"])
 187:         self.assertEqual(s_ab["stable_complementarity"]["state"],
 188:                          s_ba["stable_complementarity"]["state"])
 189:         self.assertEqual(s_ab["state"], core.SUPPORTED)   # stable ranking exists
 190:         # pair reports must be identical as a set (same named pairs, same states)
 191:         pairs_a = {(p["h1"], p["h2"], p["state"]) for p in s_ab["stable_ranking"]["pairs"]}
 192:         pairs_b = {(p["h1"], p["h2"], p["state"]) for p in s_ba["stable_ranking"]["pairs"]}
 193:         self.assertEqual(pairs_a, pairs_b)

 197:         -> complementarity REFUTED. A global-dominance reading of a ranking
 198:         result must be impossible."""
 199:         s3 = core.s3_stability(self._review_case(["bare", "a", "b"]))
 200:         self.assertEqual(s3["state"], core.SUPPORTED)
 201:         self.assertEqual(s3["stable_complementarity"]["state"], core.REFUTED)

   3: Commands:
   4:   diagnose-math [--dev-tasks N]   Run S1-S5 on the MATH-500 archive (+ judge-v2 rescore summary)
   5:   diagnose-bird                   Run S1-S5 on the BIRD phase2 archive (18 cells x arms)
   6:   controls [--phase calibration|blinded]   Freeze/run the control package, M0-M3 matrix;
   7:                                            blinded RE-EXECUTES the pre-committed challenges
   8:                                            under the current code (spec+code hash bound)
   9:   verify-challenges --challenge-result P   HISTORICAL REPLAY of a stored challenge result
  10:                                            (provenance only; never current-code validation)
  11:   inventory                       Full archive inventory rows (MATH + BIRD)
  12: 
  13: Every run writes to a fresh artifacts/diagnostics/<date>/<run_id>/ directory; frozen
  14: history is never overwritten. Offline: no model API calls.
  15: """

  40:     run_id = f"{stamp}_{tag}_{hashlib.sha256(str(time.time_ns()).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}"
